Validate and Parse Structured LLM Output Against a Coding Schema

Source: R/schema.R
validate_coded_output.Rd

Parses a JSON string (hardened against prompt-injected multi-block payloads, duplicate keys, oversized responses, control characters, and non-finite values) or validates an already-parsed R named list against an coding_schema().

Usage

validate_coded_output(x, schema, coerce = FALSE, max_bytes = 262144L)

Arguments

x

A JSON character string or a named R list.

schema

An object of class "llm_coding_schema".

coerce

Logical; if TRUE, allows safe coercion of finite numeric strings (e.g. "4.5" to 4.5) and boolean strings. Non-finite strings such as "NaN", "Inf", or "-Infinity" are always rejected. Default FALSE (strict).

max_bytes

Maximum allowed byte length of a raw JSON response string. Default 262144L (256 KiB).

Value

A list with elements:

  • valid: logical scalar indicating whether validation succeeded.

  • data: named list of validated R values (or NULL if invalid).

  • errors: character vector of validation failure messages.

Examples

s <- coding_schema(score = schema_field("integer", min = 1, max = 5))
validate_coded_output('{"score": 4}', s)
#> $valid
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $data
#> $data$score
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> 
#> $errors
#> character(0)
#> 
validate_coded_output('{"score": 9}', s)
#> $valid
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $data
#> NULL
#> 
#> $errors
#> [1] "Field 'score' (9) exceeds max (5)."
#>
